audit.summary: Valid lowest-order data make (4.9) nonunique or inconsistent; Theorem31 depends on an invalid perfect-pairing inference. VEM cohomology and DDR algebraic chains are separately supported and not declared false.
limitations: VEM potential wedge pairing is degenerate and can be inconsistent — Counterevidence: Global differential (4.6) and cohomology Theorem 30 do not use (4.9); extension (4.20) uses DDR(0) potentials. DDR proof chain unaffected by this objection.
The k=0 harmonic mode invalidates the unrestricted inf-sup claim — Counterevidence: Poincare statement (3.20) itself permits preimage zero for constant input. Theorem 14 correctly preserves H^0=R.

Adjoint-consistency estimate omits natural boundary conditions — Counterevidence: Actual mixed solution and derivative may satisfy required natural conditions through weak equations. General-dimension proof is explicitly left open, not misrepresented as supplied.
Two-dimensional radial proxy has wrong polynomial degree — Counterevidence: Formal Koszul, trimmed-space and DDR definitions use correct degree.
Two-form contraction proxy has reversed cross product — Counterevidence: Formal contraction correct; replacing all generators by their negatives preserves Koszul subspace.
Integration-by-parts rewrite has incorrect volume sign — Counterevidence: Original (2.1),(3.4), subsequent complex proof have correct signs.

proposition.claim:
Equation (4.9) defines a unique map from all VEM data to P^-_{r+1} Lambda^k; its moments imply polynomial reproduction.

Legal r=0, convex regular interval/triangle/cube, centers specified, Cartesian DOFs exactly from (4.1).

Topologically trivial Omega has trivial harmonic spaces, for k>=0, giving uniqueness and (3.21).

Nonempty connected contractible domain, unreduced de Rham complex, natural boundary weak formulation, standard zero negative-degree space.

Every sufficiently smooth omega has adjoint defect O(h^{r+1}) under additional piecewise regularity.

Omega=(0,1)^3, ell=0, r>=1, regular refining mesh, omega=dx1, mu_h=I_r^0(x1).

K_r^1 corresponds after rotation to (x-x_F)P_{r+1}.

Paper's Koszul and rotated proxy conventions, including r=0.

First-slot contraction of two-form with proxy w by v has proxy v cross w.

A.1.4 standard orientation and A.6 first-slot convention.

Rewriting (3.4) yields negative integral of d(star^-1 omega_f) plus boundary jump.

Original Stokes and DDR conventions.

repair.content:
Redesign a nondegenerate trial/test pairing compatible with desired reproduction and DOFs.

Restrict application to 1<=k<=n on contractible domain, or impose zero mean, compatible forcing and/or harmonic unknown at k=0.

Require Hilbert-adjoint domain / homogeneous normal trace tr(star omega)=0 for smooth forms, or retain boundary pairing.

Replace P_{r+1} by P_{r-1} in (2.11).

Use w cross v.

Replace volume minus by plus, retaining boundary difference as printed.
